instruction_problem: Tense not forced: 'had waited' and (less well) 'was waiting' also fit; learner cannot know which is wanted. 'was waiting' is weak (it suggests the moment of the call).
No cue word; 'In spite of' (two words) is equally right. Nothing in the task forces a contrast meaning (it is guessable, but 'Because of the rain' is not impossible sense-wise).
level_problem: Despite/in spite of is B1, low for B2.1.

instruction_problem: 'might rain' and 'should rain' are also correct after 'in case'; 'will rain' is not standard in BrE (American/informal).
Modal not fixed: would/might/could have crashed all correct.

level_problem: Reported instruction with 'not to + verb' is B1 level.

instruction_problem: 'for having been' is also correct (more formal); 'for' + -ing is not signposted but gap is clear.
Gap before 'a taxi' accepts a clause: 'suggested we take/should take a taxi' is fully correct. Task does not force -ing.
Future reference with no signal: 'starts' (timetable), 'will start', 'is going to start', 'is starting' all correct.
level_problem: Indirect question with 'start' is A2/B1, too easy for B2.2.

instruction_problem: 'was crying' also fits; 'had cried' fits less well (result vs duration). Tense not forced.
would/might/could all correct.
'weren't/wasn't' (past state, mixed conditional) is also correct: 'If I weren't so shy, I would have spoken'. Learner cannot know that only 'hadn't been' is wanted.

No cue and many linkers fit (as a result, consequently, therefore, as a consequence, hence, thus, accordingly). Only contrast linkers are wrong. 'so' after a semicolon is nonstandard but seen. Needs a first letter or fewer possible answers.
'could have' (I wish I could have more time) is also correct.
level_problem: 'I wish I had' is B1, low for B2.2.

instruction_problem: 'is running late' or 'is' + 'late': 'is' only fits the gap; fine. Other: 'is going to be' is wrong. No real second answer beyond contraction.
The cue '(have)' plus the start 'I known' nearly gives away the inversion; only the capital 'Had' needed.
'should do' is also correct (it's high time he should...); 'does' is accepted by some speakers but is less standard.
'hadn't used' fits if the phone was already used (past regret); present/future 'didn't use' is the likelier intent. Tense not forced.
'insisted that she pay/should pay' is fully correct; the gap does not force 'on paying'.
Clause answers 'we should/could go' are also correct. The cue '(go)' does not force 'to go'.
'If it weren't for your advice, I would never have applied' is correct and very common; 'hadn't been' is not the only answer.
'having seen' is also correct.
'of having sold' also correct.
Cue '(who)' is odd and misleading: 'Who wins' is wrong, 'Whoever' needs no cue; multi-word 'Anyone who' also fits the gap. A learner may type 'Who'.
'on if' is considered informal/nonstandard after a preposition; 'whether' intended. No cue.
'should go' is rare but correct after 'It's about time'.

level_problem: Very easy for B2.2 once pattern 'it's about time' is known; repeats task 30 and 33-34.

instruction_problem: Cards: only 'went' is correct; 'had gone' and 'have gone' are wrong here. Nothing else fits.
level_problem: Easy for B2.2; 'last bus leaves' context also gives the answer away only mildly.

answer: It's high time you started looking for a new job.
other_correct: It's high time you looked for a new job.
It's high time you started to look for a new job.
It's high time you found a new job.
It's high time you were looking for a new job.
It is high time you started looking for a new job.

It's high time you started job-hunting.
It's high time for you to start looking for a new job.
instruction_problem: Instruction is fine but the tense is not signposted; the 'you should' in the prompt nearly hands over the 'you ...' subject (a near-copy exercise).

level_problem: B1 level; 'would sooner' is the only B2 element.

answer: I'd rather to walk than take the bus.
sense_problem: Believable L1-transfer error; fine, but the three right sentences are short and clearly different, so the error is easy to spot.

answer: I'd rather you didn't bring your dog to the office.
other_correct: I'd rather you did not bring your dog to the office.
I'd rather you didn't bring your dog to work.
I'd rather you left your dog at home.
I'd rather you didn't bring your dog into the office.
I would rather you didn't bring your dog to the office.
